title: Mystery Shape Bag
goal: Student will describe an object's shape using at least 2 descriptive attributes (number of sides, size, curved/straight) without naming it directly.
materials: A small cloth or paper bag
5-6 familiar classroom objects or shape cutouts (circle, square, triangle, rectangle, star)
instructions: Place all shapes/objects inside the bag without the student seeing them.
Student reaches in, feels one item, and describes it out loud using shape words (round, has corners, has 3/4 sides, big/small) before pulling it out.
Peers or the clinician guess the shape based on the description.
Reveal the item and confirm or expand the description together.
Rotate turns so every student both describes and guesses.
extension: For older students, add texture and function clues ('it has 4 straight sides and we use it to check corners are square').

title: Is / Are Freeze Dance
goal: Student will produce a grammatically correct sentence using 'is' or 'are' + verb+ing to describe an action.
materials: Action cards or just open floor space
instructions: Play music; students move/dance freely.
Pause the music. Whoever is closest to the clinician must say a sentence describing what one or more classmates is/are doing (e.g., 'She is jumping,' 'They are spinning').
Clinician models and corrects verb agreement as needed (he/she/it + is; they/we/you + are).
Resume music and repeat, prompting different sentence subjects each round.
extension: Have the group vote whether the sentence used 'is' or 'are' correctly before moving on.

title: Teddy Bear Hide-and-Seek
skill: Spatial/positional concepts (in, on, under, behind, next to)
goal: Student will follow and later produce 1-2 step directions containing a positional concept with 80% accuracy.
materials: A small stuffed animal or toy
A few household/classroom items to hide it near (box, chair, book)
instructions: Clinician hides the toy while student's eyes are closed, then gives a direction: 'Look under the chair' or 'Look behind the box.'
Student follows the direction and checks the location.
After a few rounds, switch roles: student hides the toy and gives the clinician a positional direction to find it.
Track which concepts (in/on/under/behind/next to) need more practice.
extension: Add two-step directions: 'Put the bear on the box, then hide behind the chair.'

title: More or Less Snack Sort
goal: Student will correctly identify and label groups as having 'more,' 'less/fewer,' or 'the same' with 80% accuracy.
instructions: Place uneven small piles of counters on two or more plates.
Ask the student to point to the plate with 'more' or the plate with 'less/fewer.'
Have the student explain how they know (count aloud together if needed).
Adjust piles so one round has equal amounts and introduce 'the same.'
extension: Turn it into a game where the student must physically move counters to make two plates equal.

title: Story Detective: Who, What, Where, When, Why
skill: Answering WH-questions after listening to a short narrative
goal: Student will answer WH-questions about a short orally-presented story with 80% accuracy.
materials: A short 4-6 sentence original story read aloud by the clinician (create a new one each session, e.g., about a child who loses a shoe at the park)
Optional: simple drawn scene or stick-figure sketch of the story
instructions: Read the short story aloud once or twice.
Ask a mix of WH-questions: Who was in the story? What happened first? Where did it happen? When did it happen? Why did the character feel that way?
For missed questions, reread the relevant sentence and ask again.
Have the student retell the story in their own words as a wrap-up.
extension: Let the student invent the next short story and clinician asks the WH-questions back to them.

title: Whose Is It? Have/Has Scavenger Hunt
goal: Student will produce sentences using 'have' or 'has' correctly to describe ownership with 80% accuracy.
materials: 5-8 everyday objects belonging to different people in the room (backpack, water bottle, pencil case, jacket)
Optional: name tags or photos of the owners
instructions: Gather a small pile of objects that belong to different students or staff members.
Hold up one object and ask 'Who has this?' or 'Whose is this?'
Student answers in a full sentence: 'She has the backpack' or 'I have the water bottle.'
Correct have vs. has as needed based on the subject (I/you/we/they = have; he/she/it = has).
Return each object to its owner as it's identified, then rotate to a new player asking the questions.
extension: Add a memory twist: after collecting 5 objects, ask the student to recall from memory who has what without looking.
